title: Tandem Skydive Checklist
description: Recall flashcards from user-supplied course-material images; not official exam questions.
sourcePolicy: Original course answers are retained in sourceAnswer. Every card has comparison status and official references. Verified means direct substantive support in cited manuals; qualified/partially_supported do not mean prohibited. Course-only/not_found is not independent manual verification. Original question, IDs, recall format preserved. Uploaded manual editions are the baseline.

usage.grading: Recall/self-assessment; empty options and null correctOptionId. Default includeInQuiz admits only directly manual-verified cards. Show all cards in review mode; do not hide needs_review content from study.
usage.practice: Rehearse EP handle sequences with the examiner in a training harness. Canopy drills are supervised course exercises.

cards.question: What are the initial preparation tasks?
cards.answer:
Retrieve rig/student harness and move to tandem area; preflight rig; meet student; introduce yourself, ask experience and medical issues, build rapport, offer restroom opportunity.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Preflight/student preparation is supported. Twenty-minute call, restroom offer and workflow timing are course choices, not manual mandates. Generic preflight answer is not a complete itemized inspection.
Manual guidance: Perform full prescribed gear/preflight and student preparation; briefing and medical/physical suitability checks required. Local timing/rapport/restroom details remain checklist guidance.
References: OPS p.40; OPS p.38; OPS p.36; IRM p.159

cards.question: What are the harness-fitting and initial briefing tasks?
cards.answer:
Select jumpsuit if applicable; fit/tighten harness as prescribed; explain actions and where hands will touch; review exit, skydive basics and deployment once harnessed; keep student near gear-up area.

Official-manual comparison [QUALIFIED / CONTEXT]: Fitting, professional touch explanation and briefing agree in principle; actual fit must follow manufacturer details, include jumpable harness configuration before boarding and explicit post-donning check.
Manual guidance: Fit/adjust harness to manufacturer guidance, including jumpable configuration before boarding; explain personal-space contact professionally; perform immediate post-donning check; train required student tasks.
References: OPS p.34; IRM p.130; IRM p.131

cards.question: What does the checklist say about donning the rig and moving to boarding?
cards.answer:
Don and adjust rig. If rig left your sight since preflight, additional soft gear check. Move together at 5-minute call while maintaining positive student control.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Positive escort agrees. Conditional soft check when gear leaves sight does not replace mandatory post-donning check or preboarding buddy check. Five-minute timing is course-specific.
Manual guidance: Perform post-donning check regardless of whether rig remained in sight; physically escort student; obtain mandatory preboarding buddy check; use local boarding schedule.
References: IRM p.130; OPS p.42

cards.question: What checks precede boarding?
cards.answer:
Confirm boarding/exit order; maintain positive control in boarding area; check own gear and student harness just before boarding.

cards.question: What are the aircraft-entry tasks?
cards.answer:
Maintain student control; stand between student and propeller if possible; remind student to watch head; direct seating; secure both seat belts and explain operation.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Aircraft control and independent seat-belt use are supported. Exact head reminder and propeller-position technique are local checklist details, not independently verified wording.
Manual guidance: Maintain physical student supervision and secure independent seat belts; follow aircraft-specific boarding/safety briefing.
References: OPS p.43; IRM p.202

cards.question: When does this checklist remove seat belts?
cards.answer:
At 1,500 feet; check both belts completely clear of legs. This is an unverified course-checklist value.

Manual guidance: Example schedule removes belts at 1,500 feet; confirm aircraft/course schedule and ensure belts clear before exit.
References: OPS p.43; OPS p.44

cards.question: What tasks follow seat-belt removal?
cards.answer:
Hook both lower attachment points to instructor lower attachment rings; slightly tighten lower straps; complete system check including drogue; signal thumbs-up to door skydiver once complete.

Official-manual comparison [QUALIFIED / CONTEXT]: Lower hookup after 1,500 feet is optional in OPS example, whereas checklist instructs it. Early door opening requires at least one attachment before door opens.
Manual guidance: Lower hookup may occur under example schedule; ensure at least one attachment before early door opening, then all four secure for jump. Use a consistent hookup sequence.
References: OPS p.43

cards.question: What is the complete-hookup check sequence listed?
cards.answer:
Own chest/leg strap continuity and fit; tighten student back strap; tighten lowers; clip uppers; tighten uppers; check student leg buckles, loosen belly band, check chest strap; another complete systems check.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Checklist sequence is allowed as a consistent course method; OPS permits TI discretion in attachment order and additionally requires stowed running ends and full 17-point verification. IRM rubric mentions incorrect order, creating a scoring question.
Manual guidance: All four attachments secure; lowers snug, avoiding excessive tightness/looseness; ends stowed/no snags; consistent personal sequence; full 17-point system/harness verification. OPS does not mandate one attachment order.
References: OPS p.43; OPS p.44; IRM p.202

cards.question: What door and exit tasks are listed?
cards.answer:
Slide toward door while checking drogue security; set up, check drogue again, begin count; hard arch with limbs in wide X; check airspace, set drogue, check drogue; complete system check.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Generic system checks omit exact four-at-door and droguefall handle sequence; door check belongs before setting up/committing to door. Hard arch alone does not replace launch into relative wind and active flyaway. For Cat-A/B student arm assistance, IRM p.162 suggests wrist pulling, whereas OPS p.49 prohibits reaching around and pulling arms into position after drogue set; use manufacturer-specific elbow guidance/safety-position options and clarify scoring.
Manual guidance: Before door setup check both uppers, drogue and a release; final briefing/readiness/spot. Controlled launch/flyaway; visual drogue check; mandated left release, right release, cutaway, reserve, RSL, altitude check. Aim stable drogue set in 5–8 seconds.
References: OPS p.44; OPS p.47; OPS p.48; OPS p.49; IRM p.192; OPS p.49; IRM p.162
Ask evaluator: Do you expect the exact pre-door and six-item handle checks plus Cat-A/B-specific count? Will elbow guidance/safety-position retention satisfy the IRM objective instead of its wrist-pull suggestion?

cards.question: What orientation and deployment tasks are listed?
cards.answer:
Face sun if possible; turn perpendicular to jump run before deployment if possible; at 6,000 feet wave and pull drogue release. The altitude is this checklist's planned value.

Official-manual comparison [QUALIFIED / CONTEXT]: 6,000-foot planned pull is supported by IRM tandem plans. Face-sun/perpendicular-jump-run preferences are checklist choices, not universal manual requirements. Missing Cat-A/B student tasks cannot be replaced by these heading preferences.
Manual guidance: Tandem dive plans: lock on 6,500 feet; wave/pull 6,000. Air-evaluation failure floor is release below 5,000. Brief heading/traffic plan and complete category-specific student tasks.
References: IRM p.23; IRM p.31; IRM p.192
Ask evaluator: Confirm planned pull and headings, and student tasks for each category.

cards.question: What checks come immediately after deployment?
cards.answer:
Assess initial canopy; controllability check with both toggle sets; continuity check from canopy to student; turn appropriate direction; give student yellow toggles if applicable.

Official-manual comparison [DIFFERENCE FOUND]: Checklist order differs, combined-toggle wording is incomplete, and student gets toggles before comfort/penetration checks.
Manual guidance: Check/pressurize canopy, release primary toggles; establish proper heading; check flare and 90-degree left/right with primary only, then with primary+secondary; system continuity/accessibility/altitude check; adjust student; penetration check. Then optional student primary-toggle handoff, confirming lower-loop grip.
References: OPS p.50; OPS p.51

cards.question: What comfort-adjustment sequence is listed?
cards.answer:
Explain making student comfortable; use quick ejectors to remove lower straps, lengthen and promptly reattach; slightly loosen chest strap if necessary; ask student to bring knees to chest and slide back in harness.

Official-manual comparison [DIFFERENCE FOUND]: Checklist fails to specify one lower at a time or reattachment to instructor harness. Chest adjustment is more precisely incremental in OPS.
Manual guidance: Explain comfort adjustment; chest and waist loosen in one-inch increments as needed; reposition legs/sit-back drill. Release ONE lateral, fully lengthen, reattach to instructor harness; then repeat other side.
References: OPS p.51

cards.question: What final-approach and landing actions are listed?
cards.answer:
Repeat legs/feet up instruction; place instructor legs/feet under student's; flare when appropriate; assume slide landing; if winds permit ask student to stand at last moment; if catchers present ask student to open hands.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Seated landing and legs-up rehearsal agree. Wind alone does not establish stand-up suitability; seated is highly recommended for all wind conditions. Catcher instruction should include releasing toggles when catchers control brake lines.
Manual guidance: Prepare legs-up and safe flare; seated landing preferred/highly recommended in all winds. Standing/walking require appropriate speed reduction and student leg tension/preparation. With catchers, give them toggles and have student release once they control brake lines.
References: OPS p.52; IRM p.162; IRM p.203

cards.question: What closes the jump workflow?
